text: Yaskawa's ROS 2 driver that runs on the robot controller as a MotoPlus application and connects to ROS 2 through a PC micro-ROS Agent.
The open-source motion planning framework for ROS 2, giving 3D collision checking, inverse kinematics, and trajectory execution.
A MoveIt 2 library (MTC) that breaks manipulation jobs, like pick and place, into stages planned together and inspected one by one in RViz.
An ABB RAPID joint move where all joints move together, so the tool usually does not travel in a straight line to its target.
A linear move where the tool center point travels in a straight line to its target. It is written MoveL in ABB RAPID.
A MoveIt Task Constructor step that produces or connects robot states, like moving to a named pose, generating grasp poses, or attaching an object.
A prefix, such as /turtlesim1, added to a node and its relative topic names so identical nodes can run side by side without conflicts.
A single program in ROS that does one specific job, such as reading a sensor or planning a path, and communicates with other nodes.
Controlling machine tool motion with numbers stored on a medium, developed in the 1950s as a bridge between punched cards and robot programs.
A world-fixed frame where the robot's pose changes smoothly but slowly drifts.
Using motion sensors (such as wheel encoders) to estimate a mobile robot's change in position and heading over time relative to a starting pose.
Writing and testing a robot program in 3D simulation, so the real robot can keep working until the finished program is downloaded to it.
A RAPID function returning a copy of a robtarget moved by given X, Y, and Z distances (in millimeters) in the work object frame.
The company that gives leadership, maintenance, development, and support services for Nav2.
An automatic thresholding method that finds an optimal global cutoff by minimizing intra-class intensity variance on bimodal histograms.
The XML manifest file in a ROS package that lists the name, description, maintainer, software license, and dependencies needed to build and run it.
A RAPID persistent variable that keeps its last value even if the program restarts, used for taught points, tool data, and cycle counters.
A feedback control loop combining current error, accumulated past error, and error rate of change to hold a target speed or position.
An exchange of latched request and acknowledge signals (like cycle-start, busy, and done) between a PLC and robot so each knows the other's state.
A URScript function that combines two poses, converting a feature or tool frame pose into the base frame, such as computing an approach point.
The uncertainty in motion prediction caused by physical disturbances such as wheel slip and uneven terrain, represented by matrix Q in a Kalman filter.
A visual outline in Universal Robots PolyScope that displays commands, waypoints, and logic as an expandable list of steps instead of written code.
An off-delay circuit in a high-speed sensor that makes sure fast signals persist long enough for slower PLC scan cycles to detect them.
A readable, high-level programming language widely used in robotics for scripting and testing, and one of two main languages used with ROS.
An encoder arrangement with two channels offset by a quarter cycle, so the order they change shows the direction of rotation.
A signal processing technique that decodes two 90-degree phase-shifted channels (A and B) to find both rotational velocity and directional polarity.
Random Sample Consensus, an algorithm that finds geometric shapes in noisy point clouds by testing random sample points against a threshold to ignore outliers.
A named ABB RAPID code block from MODULE to ENDMODULE that holds data declarations at the top followed by PROC, FUNC, and TRAP routines.
The official Python client library for ROS 2, giving classes for nodes, publishers, subscribers, timers, and service servers.
The average distance in pixels between detected pattern points and where calibration predicts they should appear. Lower is better.
The introductory file in an open-source repository that explains what the project does, why it is useful, and how to install and run it.
A Linux kernel built or tuned (such as PREEMPT_RT or low-latency) so time-critical tasks, like a 500 Hz control loop, meet their deadlines.
An ABB RAPID function that shifts a target along tool axes, often used to compute approach and retract points from a grip point.
ROS Middleware, a software layer that connects high-level ROS 2 client libraries to communication systems like DDS or Zenoh without changing user code.
A machine that senses its surroundings, decides what to do with a program, and acts on the world, such as a six-axis factory arm.
The number of operating industrial robots per 10,000 factory workers. The International Federation of Robotics uses it to compare automation between countries.
A ROS 2 package giving non-linear state estimation through continuous, multi-sensor fused Extended and Unscented Kalman Filters.
An ABB RAPID data type that defines robot position in millimeters, tool orientation as a quaternion, arm axis configurations, and external axis positions.
Robot Operating System, an open-source middleware framework giving libraries, tools, and message-passing protocols for building robot applications.
The ROS 1 command that starts the central master nodes register with, and the global parameter server. ROS 2 has no such central server.
The command-line dependency management tool that inspects a ROS package's package.xml and installs missing system libraries through the host OS package manager.
A 3D orientation format where the vector points along the rotation axis and its length gives the angle in radians, used in URScript poses.
The fixed interval where a digital controller reads its sensor and updates its output, like the default 100 ms in the Arduino PID Library.
Selective Compliance Assembly Robot Arm: a fast, compact, usually four-axis arm that swings horizontally and is stiff vertically, used for pick-and-place and small-part assembly.
A device that measures the robot or its surroundings, like an encoder, ultrasonic range finder, or camera, for the sense, think, act loop.
Combining data from multiple sensors so the resulting estimate of a robot's position or movement has less uncertainty than any single sensor alone.
A two-way ROS communication pattern where a client node requests a server and waits for a response, used for quick one-off tasks.
A robot that does useful tasks for people or equipment outside industrial factory work, such as cleaning, delivery, inspection, or hospitality.
An RC servo protocol where shaft position is proportional to pulse width (1.0 ms to 2.0 ms) repeated every 20 ms (50 Hz).
The key that apt uses to check that software repository packages are genuine. The ROS apt package installs it with the repository configuration.
A DC circuit configuration giving a path to supply common (-).
Simultaneous Localization and Mapping, the method a mobile robot uses to build a map of an unknown room while tracking its location inside it.
A DC circuit configuration giving a path to supply source (+).
A robot wrist whose last three joint axes meet at one point, letting inverse kinematics split into a position part and an orientation part.
A program that stays in one of a fixed set of states and switches when an event happens (also called a finite state machine).
Pulsing an LED in brief flashes timed with camera exposure. This reduces heat, extends LED life, and freezes the motion of fast conveyor parts.
A placeholder in a ROS 2 launch file (such as LaunchConfiguration or FindPackageShare) whose actual value is found only when the launch file runs.
Rodney Brooks's 1986 reactive control design stacks simple behavior layers. Higher layers can suppress lower outputs while lower layers keep running.
Consistent odometry errors from robot imperfections, such as unequal wheel diameters or wheelbase uncertainty, that can be corrected by software calibration.
An optical lens whose chief rays run parallel to the optical axis, keeping constant image size and eliminating perspective error as object distance changes.
Controlling a robot remotely in real time (like the da Vinci system), so it follows a human operator rather than acting on its own.
A function s(t) that runs from 0 to 1 over a move, showing what fraction of the path is covered at each moment.
A distance measurement technique that measures the elapsed time required for emitted acoustic or optical signals to return from a target.
The working point of the tool that the robot positions, like a welding tip or gripper center. ABB default tool0 is at the flange.
The digital and analog signals and power at a robot wrist connector, used to drive and sense a gripper without cables along the arm.
The RAPID data type describing a tool: whether the robot holds it, its TCP frame, and its load (mass, center of gravity, and inertia).
A motion plan where an axis accelerates, cruises at maximum speed, and slows at the same rate, so its speed-time graph is a trapezoid.
A trapezoidal profile on a move too short to reach maximum speed: the axis speeds up and immediately slows down with no cruise phase.
The University of Michigan Benchmark test, where a robot drives clockwise and counter-clockwise squares to separate and measure wheel diameter and wheelbase errors.
The existing base ROS 2 installation or workspace (such as /opt/ros/lyrical) that an overlay workspace builds on and relies on for dependencies.
The first industrial robot, developed by George Devol and Joseph Engelberger, which began handling hot die-cast parts at a General Motors plant in 1961.
Unified Robot Description Format: an XML file that describes a robot tree of links and joints, with each joint's type, axis, position, and limits.
Using a camera and vision software to find a part, so the robot program can adjust taught points to the part's actual position.
A coordinate frame attached to a fixture or workpiece that targets are measured from, so re-teaching it moves all targets without changing the program.
Windows Subsystem for Linux version 2, a Windows tool running a Linux kernel that lets developers run Ubuntu and ROS directly on Windows.
A classic PID tuning method that finds the steady oscillation gain (Ku) and period (Pu), then calculates starting values for Kp, Ki and Kd.
